title: Model Bias Auditing
summary: Measure whether model behavior and downstream decisions differ across relevant groups, investigate causes, and validate mitigations within the actual application context.
overview: Bias auditing examines systematic differences in errors, coverage, treatment, or outcomes across relevant populations. The unit of analysis may be a model prediction, a generated summary, an agent's escalation behavior, or a complete human-assisted process. A balanced training dataset alone does not establish fair operation.

Choose metrics from the decision context and potential harms. Different fairness criteria can conflict, and protected-group data may require specific governance. Audit both the model and the workflow: unequal retrieval coverage, language quality, or reviewer behavior can create disparities even when the same model serves every user.

production.poc: A prototype should identify affected groups and plausible harms before selecting metrics. Use reviewed examples to expose obvious representational and coverage problems.
production.production: Production defines subgroup evaluation, uncertainty intervals, data handling, and an escalation path for material disparities. Keep human judgment and business policy visible in the analysis.
production.scale: At scale, monitor intersectional groups and changing populations without overinterpreting tiny samples. Reaudit after model, prompt, retrieval, policy, or user-population changes.

components.name: Audit scope
components.role: Defines the decision, affected groups, plausible harms, and relevant comparison criteria.

components.name: Governed evaluation data
components.role: Supports subgroup analysis with documented provenance and permitted attribute use.

components.name: Disaggregated metrics
components.role: Measure error, coverage, refusal, escalation, and outcome differences with uncertainty.

components.name: Investigation workflow
components.role: Separates model, data, retrieval, and process causes of observed disparities.

components.name: Mitigation review
components.role: Tests proposed changes for benefit, side effects, and remaining limitations.

flow.title: Map the decision
flow.description: Identify where model output influences people and which outcomes require comparison.

flow.title: Select groups and metrics
flow.description: Choose context-relevant dimensions under approved data-governance rules.

flow.title: Measure baseline
flow.description: Evaluate representative cases with subgroup counts and uncertainty estimates.

flow.title: Investigate disparity
flow.description: Inspect examples and trace differences to evidence, model behavior, thresholds, or human processes.

flow.title: Test mitigation
flow.description: Compare alternative prompts, data, retrieval, or workflow changes without assuming one metric captures all harms.

flow.title: Monitor recurrence
flow.description: Track deployment drift and document unresolved limitations and accountable owners.

useCase.title: Auditing an employee policy assistant
useCase.situation: A global employer offers an assistant that explains leave and workplace policies in several languages.
useCase.problem: Employees using less-represented languages receive more incomplete answers and unnecessary escalations despite equivalent questions.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must provide comparable access to accurate policy information while preserving regional policy differences.
useCase.architecture: The audit compares matched intents across languages and locations, with reviewed labels for correctness, completeness, and escalation appropriateness.
runtime: Evaluation traces reveal whether disparities arise from missing translated documents, retrieval ranking, or answer generation.
The team tests improved source coverage and retrieval before changing model prompts, then validates all affected groups.
useCase.failure: If a subgroup has too little data for a stable conclusion, the report states the uncertainty and uses targeted review rather than declaring parity.
useCase.impact: Track subgroup error and escalation rates with sample sizes, and assess whether the employee's underlying information need was met.

tradeoffs.cost: Small groups produce uncertain estimates and privacy challenges.

tradeoffs.benefit: Different harms can be examined explicitly.
tradeoffs.cost: Metrics may conflict and require accountable choices.

tradeoffs.benefit: Specific causes can be addressed efficiently.
tradeoffs.cost: Improvements for one group may create new regressions elsewhere.

failures.scenario: An aggregate improvement masks a subgroup decline
failures.detection: Disaggregated metrics show a significant direction change.
failures.recovery: Pause rollout for the affected path and investigate examples.

failures.scenario: Proxy labels encode historical unequal treatment
failures.detection: Data review finds that expected outcomes reproduce prior process bias.
failures.recovery: Reassess labels with appropriate domain and stakeholder review.

mistakes.mistake: Declaring fairness from equal overall accuracy
mistakes.fix: Examine relevant errors, coverage, and downstream outcomes.
Report counts and uncertainty instead of precise unsupported conclusions.

mistakes.mistake: Treating all disparities as model-only defects
mistakes.fix: Inspect data, retrieval, thresholds, and human decisions.

whenToUse: AI output influences access, treatment, or consequential decisions.
Users span populations with different data coverage.
The organization can govern relevant evaluation data responsibly.
whenNotToUse: A metric is selected without understanding the decision context.
Group attributes are collected without an approved purpose.
An audit is expected to certify absence of all bias.
checklist: Define affected groups and plausible harms.
Validate mitigation across all relevant segments.
Set review triggers for material changes.
